evidence_summary: Sam Ash later identifies the house-branded Fuzzz Boxx as the Astrotone-origin product made by Universal Amplifier Corp.; independent historical work documents Astrotone and Fuzzz Boxx as the same New York production family. The exact renaming chronology remains disputed because a USPTO record gives first use of the Fuzzz Boxx mark as 1967-12-31 while Sam Ash's retrospective says renamed in 1968.

evidence_summary: Specialist examination identifies the Fuzz-Stainer as a rare early-to-mid-1970s Sam Ash pedal. Surviving examples are not established as Universal Amplifier production, and one specialist account explicitly considers employee-built or locally assembled origins. Different surviving units may not share one topology, so no factory inheritance is justified.
Fuzzboxes documents Sam Ash's 1970s Fuzzola products as initially built by Shin-Ei in Japan and later by JEN in Italy. This is a separate supply branch from the Universal Amplifier Fuzzz Boxx.

Specialist Big Muff chronology identifies the JEN Jumbo Fuzz as the Italian-made product also sold as the Sam Ash Jumbo Fuzz and Sam Ash Fuzzola II. The Dallas Arbiter version is documented in a 1973 price list, providing a period anchor for the JEN family.

Independent historical sources disagree slightly on the first production year, with some placing Astrotone manufacture in 1966 and others documenting surviving 1967 examples. The archive preserves this as a production state rather than forcing a single launch year.

Later specialist comparisons report that surviving Fuzz-Stainer examples are not all built the same, with distinct topological variants. This supports treating the name as a model identity with unresolved production states rather than assigning one factory or one circuit lineage.
